 FAQ: How to watch Monday’s Canadiens-Rangers game on Sportsnet+ 
 Monday evening NHL games are exclusive to Sportsnet+ streaming in English. Here are your options if you don't have that. 
 By 
 Steve Faguy 
 November 16, 2026 at 6:00 a.m. 
 Last Updated: November 16, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. 
 On Monday, the Canadiens will play their first game of the season that’s part of the new Monday Sportsnet+ exclusive window, against the Rangers in New York at 7:30 p.m.
 Here are some frequently asked questions about how to watch the game:
 How can I watch the game?
 In English, you’ll need to subscribe to the Sportsnet+ streaming service and watch it through the Sportsnet app or website. Sportsnet has decided that Monday night national NHL games — including six Canadiens games on Mondays this season — will not be made available to Sportsnet television subscribers, unless they (or their TV providers) pay extra.
 So your options are:
 Subscribe to its direct-to-consumer streaming service Sportsnet+ , which costs $35 per month or $270 per year.
 If you have Sportsnet in your TV package with a participating provider ( you can see a list here ), sign up for the “TV Provider Add-on” that costs $13 per month.
 Subscribe to Sportsnet through Rogers cable or Rogers-owned Shaw Direct, which offer the Monday games at no additional cost.
 In French, Monday’s game — and the other five Monday Canadiens games that are exclusive to Sportsnet+ in English this season — will be on the TVA Sports channel nationally without blackouts.
 Monday’s Canadiens game against the Rangers will be exclusive to the Sportsnet+ streaming service in Canada in English. Bruce Bennett / Getty Images 
 I can stream Sportsnet through my TV provider website/app, or TV provider login on Sportsnet’s website/app. Is that enough to access the game?
 No. You need to be paying for Sportsnet+ directly or paying for Sportsnet’s TV provider add-on.
 What if I have NHL Centre Ice or Sportsnet+ Premium?
 Since the game is considered a national broadcast, the NHL Centre Ice broadcast of this game will be blacked out in Canada. If you have Sportsnet+ Premium, you can stream it using that service.
 Do I need Sportsnet+ Premium or just Sportsnet+?
 Sportsnet is making these games available as part of the standard Sportsnet+ package, so you don’t need to shell out the extra money for the premium tier.
 OK I’m subscribed. Now can I stream the game through my TV using the Sportsnet app?
 You can if your TV is a recent model Samsung TV or connected to compatible versions of one of the following devices:
 Amazon Fire TV
 Android TV
 Apple TV
 Chromecast
 PlayStation 4/5
 Xbox
 A full list of compatible devices is available on Sportsnet’s website. 
 Can I stream it with my Roku?
 No. The Sportsnet app is not available on Roku.
 What other devices can I stream it on?
 The Sportsnet app is also available on Android, iPhone and iPad, and Sportsnet+ can be streamed on a desktop or laptop computer.
 How many games this season are like this?
 Six Canadiens games this season are Monday games exclusive to Sportsnet+:
 Monday, Nov. 16, 7:30 p.m. at New York Rangers
 Monday, Nov. 23, 7:30 p.m. vs. Los Angeles Kings
 Monday, Dec. 14, 7:30 p.m. vs. Edmonton Oilers
 Monday, Jan. 4, 7:30 p.m. vs. Chicago Blackhawks
 Monday, Feb. 1, 8:30 p.m. at Vancouver Canucks
 Monday, March 22, 7:30 p.m. vs. Toronto Maple Leafs
 Are all Canadiens games on Mondays affected?
 No. Games that play in the afternoon (Jan. 18 in Buffalo and Feb. 22 in Philadelphia) or late at night (Nov. 30 in Utah and March 1 in San Jose) are not included in the national window. Those games are all regional broadcasts on TSN2 and RDS.
 What about the playoffs?
 All Canadiens playoff games should be on Sportsnet and TVA Sports. Rogers currently has no plans to make any playoff games exclusive to Sportsnet+, even if they happen on Mondays.
 What if I’m in the U.S.?
 Sportsnet’s decisions only affect viewers in Canada. In the U.S., this game will be nationally televised on TNT and TruTV, and available for streaming on HBO Max.
 What about radio?
 The Sportsnet exclusivity is only for television, so you can still listen to the play-by-play on radio, on TSN 690 in English and on 98.5 FM in French.
 Is the broadcast content different from other Sportsnet games?
 No, it’s the same Sportsnet production with the same weekday game look.
 Will there be pre-game and post-game coverage?
 Yes. But because analysis isn’t exclusive, you can also fall back on RDS’s L’antichambre or your favourite Canadiens post-game analysis show if you want.
 Can I watch highlights afterward?
 Yes. The NHL posts highlights of every game on YouTube the same night, and the league and teams post individual highlights to social media as they happen.
 Why is Sportsnet doing this?
 Money. Sportsnet’s owner Rogers is in the first season a new 12-year, $11-billion rights contract with the NHL, more than twice what it paid for its last 12-year contract. Rogers needs to make this money back somehow, and one of those ways is getting more money directly from subscribers to watch the games.

 If Rogers is offering the game to its TV subscribers, why isn’t Bell or Videotron doing the same?
 Money. Rogers said it is open to allowing other TV providers to offer the premium games to their subscribers, but to do so they would have to reach a deal that means those providers paying Rogers more money. Bell, Quebecor, Cogeco and Telus, Rogers’s direct competitors, aren’t eager to do this.
 Can Rogers do this legally?
 That will probably be up to the federal broadcast regulator or federal courts to decide. Last week, Cogeco, Eastlink and Sasktel filed a complaint with the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission arguing Rogers is engaged in “an overt, systemic strategy of market foreclosure designed to starve competing service providers of ‘must-have’ programming and systematically undermine retail competition across Canada’s broadcasting sector.”
 Rogers told Postmedia News that Rogers Cable is paying Rogers-owned Sportsnet “fair market value” to offer the games to its clients, and the complaining service providers can do the same, but have chosen not to.
 What can I do about this?
 Rogers is aware that viewers are frustrated and even outraged by this move. But the company has decided that the additional revenue is worth it. Your best bet is to vote with your wallet. If people don’t spend extra to watch the Monday games, either choosing not to watch the game, watching it in French or finding a bootlegged stream (which would be illegal and we do not endorse), it could eventually change course. You can also call your TV provider and put pressure on them to reach a deal with Sportsnet to include those games in their wholesale contract.
 Steve Faguy
